messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Spatial DGMM question
parts:
There is no error message or even a crash report from R? The whole computer? That's something...

The current release of spatialDGMM is a pure R implementation, so it is a bit slow, but shouldn't crash the system.

What are the dimensions of the dataset? (Number of pixels and number of features as given by dim()?)

Can you try subsetting the dataset to a smaller number of mass features and try SerialParam()?

It may be a parallelization issue. I expect BiocParallel to be stable, but sometimes it isn't, or sometimes there are socket connection issues.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Spatial DGMM question

Problem with parallelization using mzBin solved using this:


register(SnowParam(7, type = "MPI"))
data_bin <- mzBin(data_peaks, from=650, to=1800, resolution=50, units="ppm")
data_bin <- process(data_bin, BPPARAM=SnowParam(workers = 'MPI',
                                                            stop.on.error = TRUE,
                                                            progressbar = TRUE, RNGseed = NULL,
                                                            timeout = 30L, exportglobals = TRUE,
                                                            log = FALSE, threshold = "INFO", logdir = NA_character_,
                                                            resultdir = NA_character_,
                                                            manager.hostname = NA_character_, manager.port = NA_integer_))

All items referred above were solved. The PC didn't get BSoD screen anymore!!! Hahahahaha!
